_comment: OIDC client registry for the local stack (deploy/compose.yml), mounted at
/app/schemas/oidc/clients.json -- the path DBAL's server_routes.cpp defaults
to. The dbal image ships no clients.json of its own, so without this mount
the provider fails to initialize even with DBAL_OIDC_ISSUER set.
Only nextjs-web is registered: this stack runs exactly one app. The wider
registry (pastebin, codegen, workflowui, ...) lives in the dbal repo at
libraries/dbal/shared/api/schema/oidc/clients.json and is the source of
truth for deployments that serve more than one client.
redirect_uris are matched exactly, port included. 8080 is HTTP_PORT's
default; if you start the stack on another port, add that origin here or
/oidc/authorize will reject the callback as unregistered.
The rmacs-macbook-pro-1.taild98fe6.ts.net origin is 'tailscale serve --bg
8080' forwarding to this same nginx over a Tailscale-issued HTTPS cert --
needed because browsers only treat https://, localhost and 127.0.0.1 as a
secure context, and PKCE's crypto.subtle is unavailable outside one. A
bare Tailscale MagicDNS hostname over plain http:// will still fail.
http://0.0.0.0:8080 is registered as a convenience for local development.
It is NOT a secure context and never will be -- no browser flag or server
setting grants crypto.subtle to it. It works only because dbal-sso's
pkce.ts falls back to a JavaScript SHA-256 when crypto.subtle is absent,
which needs a redux build at or after the fallback commit; an older pin
still throws before any request reaches here. Tokens cross this origin in
plaintext HTTP, so keep it to a laptop. Note DBAL_OIDC_ISSUER still
defaults to the localhost origin: the browser flow stays on 0.0.0.0
because dbalOidcBase is the relative /api/dbal, but the minted 'iss' claim
will read localhost. Override DBAL_OIDC_ISSUER to the 0.0.0.0 origin if
anything ever starts validating it.
